extracted.intended_audience: Area chairs and meta-reviewers for ACL/EMNLP-style academic conferences (conference program chairs, senior area chairs, and first-time ACs)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for area chairs/meta-reviewers on responsibilities, time management, communication, and a template/criteria for writing meta-reviews for NLP conferences (ACL/EMNLP-style).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role responsibilities of an Area Chair / Meta-Reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible for looking through the initial reviews (usually three), making a recommendation whether the paper is ready to be published, and writing a short so-called meta-review summarizing the major points of the reviews as well as the reviewers’ discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs should synthesize reviews and discussions, act as a safety net for reviewer mistakes/omissions, and provide the program committee (PC) with a concise summary that supports decisions beyond raw scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time commitment and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-reviewing is time-intensive: checking reviewer assignment (~10 minutes per paper), reading reviews and initiating discussion (~30 minutes per paper average), and writing meta-reviews (at least 45 minutes per paper; can be 1–2+ hours for difficult cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Block full days in your calendar when reviews/responses arrive; expect several days of work for a batch of papers. Conference organizers should allow more time for thorough meta-reviewing (suggested: two weeks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Check reviewer assignment for problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Check potential problems in reviewer assignment, around 10 minutes per paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify conflicts of interest, mismatches in expertise, or other assignment errors early and flag them to SAC/PC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiate and manage reviewer discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: As the reviews and author responses come in, start a discussion among reviewers, at least in cases where you want further opinions or want reviewers to elaborate/discuss their points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read all reviews thoroughly before prompting discussion; use discussions to resolve disagreements or request clarifications; devote ~30 minutes per paper on average to this step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review structure (template)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested meta-review template sections: SUMMARY; STRENGTHS and CONTRIBUTIONS; WEAKNESSES; WRITING; REVIEWS and DISCUSSION; SUMMARY (final evaluation); ADDITIONAL COMMENTS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this template as a flexible guide; adapt for specific paper types but include these components to make the meta-review useful for authors, AC/SAC, and PC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review: Opening summary
rubrics_metrics.description: 2–3 sentences (but no more) summarizing what the paper is about, as usual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise and clear; do not restate the paper's contributions list verbatim—summarize the core idea for context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review: Strengths and contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: State the reasons to accept the paper; note the points you consider real contributions rather than repeating the paper's own contributions list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on what is novel, important, or convincing about the work; be specific so authors and PCs understand the basis for positive assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review: Weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: List things to be improved, especially for rejected papers—for instance, methodological flaws or missed comparisons with particular prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When identifying missing comparisons, keep in mind what was published by the submission deadline; explain why a weakness matters for acceptance or requires revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review: Writing quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on whether the writing is clear enough or needs improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out unclear sections or presentation issues that could be fixed in a revision; distinguish stylistic problems from substantive flaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review: Reviews and discussion summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize what the reviewers recommend, especially what happened in the reviewers' discussion. Keep the summary double-blind and possibly add information received via the author response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a neutral synthesis of reviewer positions, note key disagreements and how they were resolved (if at all), and incorporate relevant points from the author response without breaking anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review: Final evaluation summary (avoid explicit recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a summary evaluation of the paper (e.g., 'needs only minor modifications' or 'would profit from another iteration') but do not explicitly state your accept/reject recommendation in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PC decisions may differ; the meta-review should characterize the paper's readiness and remaining issues rather than giving a direct accept/reject command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional comments when disagreeing with reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases where you disagree with initial reviews, especially when recommending rejection or when agreeing only with some reviewers, state points that make clear you took a closer look at the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give concrete reasons and evidence for your disagreement (e.g., 'one reviewer asked for X, but in my view this is beyond the scope of the paper') so SAC/PC can understand your judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a safety net—dig deeper when reviewers are inexperienced
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that many reviewers may be relatively new and not all initial reviews are reliable; ACs should dig deeper (look up prior work, sometimes almost write a review themselves) when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you find merit the reviewers missed, justify it with citations or succinct analysis to persuade SAC/PC; don't defer to reviewers blindly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and usefulness of feedback to authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide polite and useful feedback, especially because many submissions come from PhD students and junior researchers who deserve constructive guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even for rejected papers, aim to explain why and what next steps would help; keep feedback respectful and actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take sides when appropriate for mixed reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs have more time than SACs; do not be afraid to take sides in weighing pros and cons for papers with mixed reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state why you weigh some reviewer concerns more heavily than others to help SAC/PC make informed decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain double-blind integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the meta-review keeps the process double-blind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When summarizing reviews and author response, avoid language that could reveal identities and do not include non-public identity information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect relevant publication cutoff dates
rubrics_metrics.description: When judging novelty or missing comparisons, keep in mind what has already been published at the submission deadline of your conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not penalize authors for work published after the submission deadline; frame prior-work expectations relative to that cutoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely communication with SAC/organizers
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate in a timely fashion with Senior ACs (SACs) and organizers—e.g., send brief updates if you haven't finished yet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even a short message ('I haven't gotten to this yet but I will tomorrow') helps coordination across many ACs and prevents delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to conference organizers: allow more meta-review time
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference organizers should allow more time for thorough meta-reviewing in the future (suggested: two weeks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer time windows reduce rushed judgments and improve review quality; consider scheduling and workload when assigning AC duties.
